transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Time: 15:00 PT (52m)
Title: Ironwood Analytics - Private VPC Architecture Discovery
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sarah Morales (CTO), Jorge Alvarez (Network), Maya Singh (Security), Tom Bates (ML Platform), Nina (PM)

[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time, really appreciate it. Quick agenda — we want to understand Ironwood's networking constraints, region needs, and compliance items so we can propose the right Private (VPC) deployment. Priya will dig into the topology stuff.

[00:18] Sarah (Ironwood CTO): Thanks, Liam. To start, our key asks: inference latency under 50ms p50 for short prompts, data must not leave eu regions for EU customers, and we need audit logs pushed into our SIEM. We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private but leaning Private for control and compliance.

[00:34] Priya (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say 'data must not leave eu regions' — is that for storage at rest only, or both transit and inference execution?

[00:44] Maya (Security): Both if possible. We need model evaluation and tokens processed for EU customers to remain in eu-west-1. For US records it's fine to be us-east-1. Also KMS should be customer-managed.

[01:02] Jorge (Network): One practical constraint — we have VPCs across two accounts in AWS: our prod account and our infra account. We also use a Transit Gateway for cross-account routing. Any Redwood setup needs to play nicely with TGW or we prefer VPC peering if simpler.

[01:18] Priya (SE): Okay, good context. Quick note: Redwood Private supports both patterns — direct VPC peering and interface endpoints/private endpoints via endpoint services. Peering is sometimes simpler but has transitive routing limitations; TGW can centralize it but there are attachments and route table considerations.

[01:35] Tom (ML Platform): For performance, we probably want the serving pods in the same AZs as our data egress points to minimize cross-AZ latency. What's Redwood's recommendation on AZ pinning?

[01:50] Priya: We can pin nodes to specific AZs. Our runtime supports AZ affinity; kernels are optimized and we usually colocate with customer endpoints to hit the latency SLOs. That said, cross-AZ hops add ~2-4ms typically, but depends on your overlay.

[02:10] [Speaker 2 - background murmurs]

[02:25] Jorge: Regarding IP space. We have overlapping /16s in older accounts — messy. We can't do peering if there's CIDR overlap. Any guidance?

[02:34] Priya: Overlap is a blocker for classic peering. Workarounds: use TGW with route propagation and NAT+SNAT, or set up PrivateLink (interface endpoints) where IPs are from the consumer VPC and the endpoint is an ENI, which avoids peering collision. There's also AWS RAM or AWS Network Manager but those are heavier.

[02:55] Sarah: Is PrivateLink supported for Redwood Private? How do credentials and auth work over that?

[03:05] Liam: Yes, we support PrivateLink/interface endpoints as part of Redwood Private. Authentication is mutual TLS between our control plane and the endpoint; for the data plane we use mTLS and customer-managed KMS can be integrated for envelope encryption. We'll share docs.

[03:25] Maya: We need to see the KMS integration details. HSM-backed keys are a must for some datasets. Any HSM / Cloud KMS caveats?

[03:34] Priya: Redwood can accept CMKs (customer-managed keys) in AWS KMS; HSMs via Cloud HSM are possible but require additional ops. For on-prem HSMs you'd need a VPC link and a proxy for key wrapping; that's more custom. We'll call out the differences in the diagram.

[03:52] Nina (PM): On the pilot — what would you need from us to do a quick latency and correctness run?

[04:00] Liam: Minimal: a sample prompt set (10-20), example model size you'd like (we can propose a 7B first), and a target region. We'll spin up a small cluster in your VPC or via PrivateLink, run load and latency tests, and share traces.

[04:15] Tom: We want to test eu-west-1 first. Can Redwood deploy into customer-managed VPCs in eu-west-1?

[04:23] Priya: Yes, we have deploy targets in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Deployment model options: 1) Redwood agents in your VPC with interface endpoints to our control plane, 2) Redwood-managed nodes attached to your VPC via peering or TGW. Option 1 gives you maximum control and isolation.

[04:44] Jorge: If we do option 1 (agents in our VPC), what's the maintenance surface? Patching, upgrades, who does kernel upgrades?

[04:54] Priya: Generally, Redwood manages runtime upgrades but we can coordinate maintenance windows. Agents run as containers/instances under your account; Redwood will push updates using our agent controller with an RBAC model. You retain access and can opt-out of automatic upgrades if required.

[05:12] Maya: Audit logs — we need all inference requests and decisions logged and forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk). Is there a log forwarder?

[05:22] Liam: Yes, we can forward structured logs to your S3 with encryption and from there to Splunk, or send directly to an HTTPS collector. Logs can include token-level cost breakdowns but we can strip PII. We'll provide retention and filtering configs.

[05:40] [00:05 silence, keyboard clacking]

[05:50] Sarah: On networking limits — Transit Gateway has attachment quotas. If we need many VPCs attached, will Redwood advise on scale patterns?

[05:59] Priya: We'll propose a hub-and-spoke with TGW for many VPCs; for smaller footprint we'd lean to PrivateLink to avoid TGW complexity. Also note TGW propagation to multiple route tables needs careful planning for security boundaries.

[06:18] Jorge: Any issues with peering across accounts in other regions? We have a cross-region requirement for DR in us-east-1.

[06:27] Priya: Cross-region peering exists but there's cost and latency. For DR, common pattern is replicate minimal model cache to us-east-1 region and fallback routing — Redwood supports cross-region model replicas and automatic routing fallback. We'll include a suggested failover diagram.

[06:45] Tom: About IP egress — does Redwood require NAT gw for outbound internet calls?

[06:52] Priya: Outbound depends on your deployment choice. If you're fully in VPC with no egress allowed, we support pulling container images via VPC endpoints to ECR; if egress is restricted, plan for endpoint services or an internal registry mirror.

[07:10] Maya: Compliance question — do you have SOC2 report and penetration test summaries we can review?

[07:16] Liam: Yes, we'll share our SOC2 attestation and a redacted pen test summary under an NDA. We'll attach links in the follow-up email and point to specific controls for data handling.

[07:30] Nina: Timeline — if we decide to pilot next week, how long to get infra ready?

[07:36] Priya: If we get CIDRs and account IDs today, we can produce a deploy plan in 3 business days and run a pilot within 7-10 business days, assuming access is granted.

[07:49] Sarah: One more — how is service mesh or sidecar handled? We already have Istio in prod; can Redwood integrate?

[07:56] Priya: We can integrate with existing mesh but usually we run our own sidecars for inference traffic to ensure token-level observability; however, we can conform to your mTLS & tracing headers. We'll detail integration patterns.

[08:12] [brief crosstalk]

[08:20] Liam: Recap, agreed items: Redwood to share VPC/endpoint diagrams, KMS/HSM notes, SOC2 docs, and a pricing pilot baseline. Ironwood to share VPC CIDRs, account IDs, and preferred regions. We'll book a pilot planning call next week.

[08:36] Sarah: Sounds good. One ask: can you call out the differences in model quantization impact on latency — would 4-bit quantization be recommended for us?

[08:45] Priya: Yes, for throughput cost tradeoffs we'll recommend quantization profiles per model size. 4-bit can reduce memory and cost but may slightly affect qual; we'll run a QoE check during pilot.

[08:58] Jorge: Also, we have VLAN overlap between the EU and US network. We'll try to clean it up but if not possible, PrivateLink is probably the path.

[09:08] Liam: Noted. We'll include both peering and PrivateLink diagrams. Any other blockers?

[09:12] Maya: Just the KMS/HSM specifics and the SOC2 evidence.

[09:18] Liam: Okay we'll get those out today or tomorrow. Appreciate the time, everyone.

[09:25] [meeting closes - informal goodbyes]
